speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a significant medical history and are presenting with gait and limb ataxia. To understand the underlying cause, please describe your specific symptoms, how long they have persisted, and any recent changes in your condition. Additionally, please list your complete medical history and current medications.

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds like significant ataxia; does your clumsiness worsen when you close your eyes (positive Romberg sign), and have you noticed any speech difficulties, swallowing problems, or limb weakness? Also, please confirm if you have a history of stroke, multiple sclerosis, or alcohol use disorder, as these are critical for narrowing the differential.

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to Natalizumab therapy.

REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with and without contrast.
REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain showing white matter lesions.

The combination of unexplained ataxia and a history of Crohn's disease treated with natalizumab is highly concerning for PML, an opportunistic infection of the central nervous system. We need immediate neuroimaging to confirm this diagnosis.
